PullRequest.Title: Chat: open agent session links at their linked request (proposed by opus 5.5)
PullRequest.Body:

* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests

Proposed implementation for #349148.

Part 2 of 3 for cross-host agent request search (#349134 host index, #349136 client search). This PR is independent of the other two, but agent request search uses it to open a result at the matching request.

## What changes

`agent-host-session://` links can already carry `turn=<id>`, but both link openers ignored it. Opening a link with a turn now focuses that request and scrolls it to the top of the transcript. This works in:
- the Agents window, for in-window links, chat windows, and links handed over by the OS
- the editor window

Details:
- **Restored chats.** If the chat is restoring its history, the reveal waits up to 15 seconds, the same limit the Agents window already uses to wait for a linked session.
- **Missing turns.** A turn the chat no longer shows, for example one removed by editing an earlier request, leaves the chat where it opened.
- **Stale reveals.** Opening another link, or moving focus to another chat, stops the wait, so a slow chat never takes focus from the one the user moved on to.

## How it changes

- **`revealChatRequest`** (`chat/browser/widget/chatRequestReveal.ts`) polls until the widget renders the request, then calls `IChatWidget.reveal(item, 0)`.
  - It confirms the request is rendered by focusing it and checking `getFocus`.
  - `reveal` gains an optional `relativeTop` argument.
  - It stops on cancellation or timeout, or when `onDidChangeFocusedWidget` reports another chat.
- **`revealLinkedTurn`** (`sessions/contrib/chat/browser/chatLinkRouting.ts`) serves both Agents window paths.
- **Each opener keeps one pending reveal.** It clears the reveal at the start of every open. It assigns a new reveal only if no newer open has started since, using a generation counter in the openers and the handoff's cancellation token.
- **Docs.** `src/vs/sessions/SESSIONS.md` describes the `turn` behavior.

## How to test

1. Copy an agent session link that has a `turn` from an agent's output, or build one with `buildOpenSessionLinkUri(session, chat, turnId)`.
2. Open it in the Agents window, then in the editor window. The chat opens scrolled to that request, even if the chat was not loaded.

Targeted tests:
- `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\chat\test\browser\openSessionLinkOpener.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\agentSessions\agentHost\openSessionLinkOpener.contribution.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\chat\test\electron-browser\agentsWindowWorkspaceHandoff.test.ts` — 49 passing.
- With the opener changes stashed, the two new reveal tests fail (2 failing). They cover:
  - revealing once the transcript renders
  - a later link that has no turn, or that fails to open
  - focus moving to another chat

I did not try this in a running window with real restored chats.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a session link in the Agents main window, including side-by-side chats.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session lookup, optional default-chat resolution, and the existing openChat/openChatToSide/openSessionToSide operation complete before reveal starts. A ready request is focused and revealed synchronously once; otherwise the reveal runs without awaiting its polling promise.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the cached session subscription, falling back to connection.listSessions to identify the default chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero listing calls with a session subscription or without an explicit chat ID; otherwise one listing call per resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same resolveLinkedChat call and cache/listing fallback already ran before this PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore an uncached chat using hydrated session/chat subscriptions and history conversion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider content resolution per uncached chat, coalesced by resource in ChatService and ChatSessionsService; cached models avoid resolution. Existing history enrichment remains unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening the same chat already restored its model and history through these services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing restoration must make the transcript available before a request can be revealed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Focus the matched transcript item and reveal it through the virtualized list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful focus/reveal per link with a rendered matching request; failed hasElement checks do not focus or reveal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Links opened the chat without request-specific focus or scroll.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The immediate attempt runs synchronously after opening; later attempts run on interval callbacks.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One linked chat per activation; session lookup scales with known sessions, and reveal lookup scales with visible transcript items H. Unsuccessful reveal checks run every 100 ms for at most 15 seconds.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One pending reveal per in-window opener, replaced on subsequent opens; generation checks suppress older completed opens. Existing session/model resolution remains coalesced by resource. Poll callbacks are synchronous and do not spawn concurrent boundary operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: getWidgetBySessionResource scans registered widgets in memory. ChatViewModel.getItems caches its computed visible array until a model change; polling does not restore history, list sessions, or copy that array on each tick. Links without a turn allocate no reveal timer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced routing, default-chat fallback, model-load coalescing, visible-item caching, and list focus/reveal implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Transcript lengths and restoration durations are unmeasured; the repeated work is a bounded in-memory search rather than boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added request navigation is demand-driven and bounded, with no increase in existing restore or listing call cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate a session link from an auxiliary chat window.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing chat-window resolution and open/reveal complete first. The new helper then finds the widget and reveals its request; asynchronous waiting is not awaited by the opener.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve an explicit chat ID through cached subscription state or the existing session-listing fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one fallback listing for this resolution, not one per transcript item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical default-chat resolution preceded the same chat-window open.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve or activate the destination chat in an existing auxiliary window and mount its chat editor when necessary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical open; concurrent identical opens are coalesced and operations for the same requested chat are queued. Existing destination chats are revealed rather than recreated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same openLinkedChatInChatWindow operation and destination reuse ran before the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire a cached model or load provider-backed chat content for a newly mounted destination.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero provider loads for a retained model; one coalesced load per uncached resource, with existing provider-owned history work unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The destination chat editor already acquired or loaded the same model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: History availability gates eventual request reveal.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One destination chat per activation, registered widget count W, and destination transcript item count H.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing chat-window single-flight and per-chat queue remain intact. Reveal is limited to one pending operation for this opener and stops on success, replacement, cancellation, another focused widget, or timeout.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The window service reuses chats by URI; SessionsChatWindowContent also reuses resolved chat entries. The new widget and transcript searches are in-memory and use the view-model visible-items cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected window-service grouping, provider chat reuse, model coalescing, and the reveal helper.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Widget count, history size, and cold restoration duration vary; no additional subprocess, filesystem, database, or network operation is initiated by polling.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression. The added work does not recreate windows or repeat remote restoration.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an agent-session turn link in the editor window's Chat view or chat editor.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing client identity resolution, default-chat normalization, provider activation, and openSession complete before reveal. A ready transcript is revealed once; polling does not extend the awaited open operation by the timeout duration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List sessions when the client/backend identity is not known.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero on an identity-cache hit; one in-flight listing per authority on a miss, shared by concurrent resolutions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same authority-keyed refresh map, listing call, and registration loop already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before provider activation and openSession.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use the subscription cache or listSessions fallback to normalize an explicit default-chat ID.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero listing calls with a hydrated session or no fragment; otherwise one fallback call. A cold identity lookup can separately have its own unchanged listing call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Normalization and its possible separate listing call were already on this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reuse an open widget or load the provider-backed model through its existing host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical openSession in either configuration branch; zero provider loads for retained models, otherwise a resource-coalesced load.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each branch already called openSession exactly once with the same target and options.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing open/restore gates widget availability; additional polling is fire-and-forget.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One session/chat per link; a cold identity refresh handles the selected authority's session listing, while request lookup scans H visible transcript items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One pending reveal for this contribution; a generation counter prevents an older open from installing a reveal after a newer open. Model and content resolutions remain shared by resource; distinct existing opens are not newly globally serialized or fanned out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Identity cache and per-authority refresh sharing are unchanged. Existing widget/model/content caches remain effective. getItems returns its cached visible array between changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both pre/post branches perform the same single openSession and unchanged identity/default-chat resolution.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings were measured. The immediate new work is an in-memory lookup and one requested focus/scroll, not another host listing or content request.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression or concrete pre-existing performance regression fixed by this refactoring.

Scenarios.Scenario: Follow a turn link delivered by the OS to the Agents window, including cold startup and a disconnected provider.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing LifecyclePhase.Restored readiness, session availability, optional provider connection, default-chat resolution, and chat opening must complete. Reveal is installed afterward without awaiting its promise.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC event per external open intent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same handler received and processed the external session link.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Starts the workflow; no new IPC is issued by reveal polling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Optionally connect the session's provider, resolve its default chat, and restore/open the destination through the existing services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one explicit provider.connect invocation when disconnected, one default-chat listing fallback when required, and the existing resource-coalesced content load for the target chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Connection, resolution, and opening occurred in the same order before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing operations precede reveal and can dominate cold startup latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One linked session and chat per handoff. Existing session availability checks react to provider/resolution events; new reveal checks only the destination widget/transcript.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The handoff's cancellation token rejects superseded completions; its MutableDisposable retains one reveal. In-app and OS routing have separate owners, so the Agents window can have one reveal from each, not unbounded reveals per link. Both are time-bounded.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Known sessions and connected providers bypass their existing waits/connect step. Default-chat subscription and chat-model caches retain their behavior. The new reveal never forces a reconnect or history reload on a missing request.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected the IPC handler, cancellation ownership, session-availability wait, connection branch, and new reveal placement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold provider connection/history duration is environment-dependent but unchanged; the diff introduces no new startup-wide fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression. The extra 15-second deadline is not an awaited startup delay.

Scenarios.Scenario: A linked request is missing, history renders late, or a later open/focus change supersedes the reveal.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: There is no awaited 15-second delay in the callers. Interval callbacks perform in-memory searches until success, cancellation, another focused chat, or timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit a trace diagnostic after an uncancelled unsuccessful reveal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one diagnostic per timed-out reveal, conditional on the logging sink's trace handling; not one per poll or transcript item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after the asynchronous wait settles, not as a prerequisite to opening the chat.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Approximately 150 retry opportunities at most per pending reveal, each scanning up to W widgets and H visible transcript items. A present item not yet in the list receives only a guarded hasElement check; a successful focus/reveal terminates retries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One timer and deadline per pending reveal owner. DisposableStore disposes the interval, timeout, cancellation subscription, and focus subscription on finish. Replacement/disposal cancels the previous owner; generation checks prevent accumulating stale reveals.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Visible-item computation is cached until a model change; unsuccessful polling does not invalidate it or allocate a new history/model. There is no negative-result cache, but retries have a fixed deadline and do not cross host boundaries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for bounded retry count, cache behavior, and cleanup: inspected ChatViewModel.getItems, ChatWidget.focus, ChatListWidget.focusItem, IntervalTimer disposal, and cancellation-token ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large transcripts increase total scan work, but static evidence does not establish a meaningful degradation from this bounded, cached-array search. No unbounded retained collection or expensive per-poll operation was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable high-confidence performance regression. Missing-turn handling adds bounded local work, not repeated restore/I/O or lifetime-growing retention.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all 10 changed files and all diff pages against base bfbaab8611c6df0f12d176833f08091ee22a5bb0. Traced added polling/focus work, cancellation and retention, cold/warm identity and model caches, native handoff, auxiliary-window grouping, and unchanged host boundaries. No findings meet the required performance evidence threshold; no concrete regression-fix provenance signal was identified. Static review only; duration and prevalence remain unmeasured.
